messages:
Maya Patel: quick report — ran into another flaky retry case in our Kotlin sample: streaming request + 401 during body write -> okhttp logs 'retry suppressed' and user sees EOF. Repro is easy on flaky network emulators.
Alex Chong: saw that earlier. Is this the one where auth refresh happens mid-write and our RetryInterceptor does chain.proceed(newReq)?
Maya Patel: yeah. Snippet of logs:
```
D/OkHttp: --> POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/complete
I/Network: streaming body write started
W/Network: connection reset during write
I/Auth: token refresh triggered
I/Auth: token refresh complete
D/OkHttp: attempting retry with new token
E/OkHttp: retry suppressed: request body is not repeatable
E/SDK: call failed: java.io.EOFException: unexpected end of stream
```
Diego Ruiz: note: interceptors operate on the same Call. If the RequestBody is one-shot (streaming) chain.proceed() will consume it. There's no automatic seek/rewind for RequestBody.
Alex Chong: agreed. We need to update sample app guidance and SDK behavior. Proposed short-term fixes: 1) sample app buffers small payloads (<=128KB) into repeatable request bodies; 2) quickstart docs mention non-repeatable bodies won't be retried and show how to prefetch/refresh token.
Maya Patel: long-term SDK options: expose builder flag enableBufferedRetries(maxBytes) (opt-in). Behavior: if enabled and body size <= maxBytes, buffer into memory and replay on retry; otherwise fail with clear error. Also emit telemetry event 'retry_suppressed_non_repeatable' with payload_size and device info.
Diego Ruiz: agree on opt-in. Default should be fail-fast with actionable diagnostics so mobile apps don't OOM silently. Also add an explicit error type like NonRepeatableBodyException with message: "Request body is not repeatable; either buffer it or enable SDK buffered retries (docs link)."
Maya Patel: alternative mitigation: preemptive auth refresh. AuthInterceptor could check token expiry before writing body and refresh synchronously if TTL < threshold. That avoids mid-flight 401s but adds cost. Include sample snippet in quickstart: 
```
// simple preemptive check
if (AuthManager.tokenExpiringSoon()) { AuthManager.refreshSync() }
chain.proceed(request)
```
Alex Chong: also tested Expect: 100-continue approach briefly; server didn't send 401 before client started streaming on our mock, so not reliable. Document as experimental.
Diego Ruiz: test plan: add MockWebServer CI test that closes connection mid-body to assert two behaviors: buffered path succeeds with retry, non-buffered path fails with NonRepeatableBodyException and emits telemetry. Add an instrumentation test on Pixel emulator to validate memory footprint.
ci-bot: created issue RD-INF-8012: "android-sdk: opt-in buffered retries + diagnostics for non-repeatable request bodies during auth refresh" and attached logs.
Maya Patel: I'll update the Kotlin sample and quickstart with code examples and link to the new issue. Alex, can you own the MockWebServer test?
Alex Chong: yep. I'll add a small util in tests:
```
// Mock server: respond with 200 but close socket during request body
mockWebServer.enqueue(MockResponse().setSocketPolicy(SocketPolicy.DISCONNECT_DURING_REQUEST_BODY))
```
Maya Patel: thanks. Let's keep the buffering opt-in and show recommended heuristics (128KB default). Also add a short note in the onboarding checklist: "If you expect retries on 401, ensure request bodies are repeatable or enable buffered retries." :thumbsup:
